analysis.reading:
THE CAPTURE THAT CORRECTED TWO OF MY FINDINGS, NOW READ FOR ITS CITATIONS. Supplied by MANUS on 12 August as ground truth, it carries five complete source cards and seven inline citations with resolvable URLs — which is how it overturned my claims that in-text citations mostly flatten and that most attribution is lost to scroll.

Read for content, it is a clean instance of adoption with the author erased. The essay supplies the concept: topology over text, the reader’s path as the poem. Its Zenodo record is card 2 and is cited inline four times. Card 1, scienceaijournal.com, carries the full title AND the CERN/Zenodo provenance — so an aggregator preserved the institutional chain while dropping the person. Three cards are genuine prior art: Wikipedia on net-poetry, the Oxford Review of Books on poetry-writing AI, and the University of Toronto’s Representative Poetry Online. The field is real and the archive’s contribution sits inside it, unattributed.

observation.transcript:
"The network is the poem" is a modern concept in digital literature and computational poetics. It suggests that the true meaning of a poem comes from its structure and connections (its network or topology) rather than the exact words on the page. [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20220299), [2](https://scienceaijournal.com/topics/digital-humanities-and-scholarship-t12377), [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net-poetry)]

Here is how this idea changes how we look at poetry:

Key Ideas

* Topology over Text: The arrangement of ideas and how they link together matters more than the quality of the individual lines. [1](https://zenodo.org/records/20220299)
* AI and Algorithms: This concept is often used to analyze poetry generated by artificial intelligence. It looks at how AI models connect different ideas, themes, and words. [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20220299), [2](https://www.facebook.com/this.is.the.ORB/videos/orb-lecture-series-tracey-guiry/344256657096311/)]
* Interactive Reading: In digital poetry, the reader clicks through links or nodes. Each reading path creates a unique network and a unique poem. [1](https://rpo.library.utoronto.ca/content/online-editors-introduction)

Why It Matters

* Deeper Analysis: It helps scholars map out complex themes in long epics or large collections of poetry.
* New Creativity: It allows poets to build interactive, web-based poems where the experience changes for every visitor.

You can explore this concept further by reading the open-access essay on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/20220299), which explores why network structure matters more than text quality in the age of AI. [1](https://zenodo.org/records/20220299)

If you want to explore this more, tell me:

* Are you interested in AI-generated poetry or interactive digital poetry?
* Would you like to see an example of how a poem can be mapped as a network?

Let me know what sparked your interest!
